deep.reconstruction: There is no mathematics on this page. It is a library request or loan slip (Leihzettel), most likely from the Göttingen University Library. In ink it reads: '[L]iouville. Journal de mathématiques. T. 17. Paris 1852 / T. 18. Paris 1853. / T. 20. Paris 1855.' At the bottom right is the signature 'B Riemann', with a parenthetical word beneath it. That word is hard to read. It may be a street or address designation, or the name of a messenger or servant; the transcription's 'Weg̃str.' is doubtful. Around these are library and archival marks: a large '33' in pencil with a pencil cross-stroke (probably a shelf or processing mark), pencil underlinings under the volume numbers, a faint pencil mark at the right margin, and a red-pencil note at the left. The red note reads something like 'Nov. 4. 58' or 'Nr. 4. 58'. If it is a date, it would place the loan around November 1858. That reading is uncertain. The next folio is a parallel slip for the same three volumes, possibly with other names, so these are probably duplicate or companion loan records. Possible relevance, which is my inference and not on the page: volume 17 (1852) of Liouville's Journal contains Chebyshev's two memoirs on the distribution of primes. These are 'Sur la fonction qui détermine la totalité des nombres premiers inférieurs à une limite donnée' and 'Mémoire sur les nombres premiers'. Those memoirs are directly pertinent to Riemann's 1859 paper on the number of primes. However, the slip names no articles, so it cannot be said which papers Riemann wanted from these volumes. Nothing in the slip itself establishes a connection to his 1859 work.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a library slip with no mathematical content. It is mildly interesting as evidence of Riemann's reading. If the red note is a date (Nov. 1858) and the volume 17 request was for Chebyshev's prime-number memoirs, it would bear on the background of his 1859 prime paper. Both of those points are speculative, and Riemann's familiarity with the French journal literature is unsurprising.
transcription_corrections: The first word's initial letter is obscured by an ink blot; 'Liouville' is the right reading.
The parenthetical under the signature is not clearly 'Weg̃str.'. It looks more like '(Wißtel.)' or a similar short word, and should be marked illegible or uncertain.
The large pencil '33' and the long pencil cross-stroke are library or archival marks, not Riemann's writing.
The red-pencil note at the left is better read as a possible date, 'Nov. 4. 58' (or 'Nr. 4. 58'), than as part of the text. It is in a different hand or medium.
There is a small faint pencil mark at the right margin next to 'T. 20. Paris 1855', possibly 'K5' or 'KS'. It is omitted in the transcription.
